title: [core][misc] simply output processing with shortcut code path

experiments.name: output_processing_shortcut_throughput
experiments.workload: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B on H100, benchmark_throughput.py input-len 256 output-len 256; mean of 3 trials.
experiments.note: Diff adds an n==1 and not use_beam_search shortcut in _process_sequence_group_outputs (single_step.py) that appends the single token, detokenizes, stop-checks and frees inline, skipping the general child-sequence/beam machinery. Number source: comment trials main mean ~24.24 -> PR mean ~24.62 req/s (~1.5%).

reported.scope: end-to-end Llama-3-8B serving throughput (GPU-bound), where the CPU output-processing shortcut the diff adds is a tiny fraction of per-step time
reported.scale_short: Author's req/s is whole-model Llama-3-8B serving; the diff only shortcuts the CPU output-processing path. TO MAKE 1:1: microbench _process_sequence_group_outputs alone for the n==1 non-beam case, general path vs shortcut, on CPU.
reported.scale_note: SAME unit (req/s) but 24.24 -> 24.62 is GPU-bound E2E Llama-3-8B throughput; the output-processing shortcut is a CPU-path win nearly hidden by model compute, hence only ~1.5%. Isolated on CPU the relative savings of skipping the child-seq/beam machinery is larger. Direction genuine; magnitude diluted by GPU work.

environment: reported-only: author's published numbers; measured arms pending on GPU box
